propositions: Long-running LLM gate operations (transition closed, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no output to stdout/stderr between invocation and final verdict, routinely exceeding 600s supervisor stall watchdog budgets

Autonomous agents invoking gate operations get killed by stall watchdogs unable to distinguish healthy long-running calls from hung processes, leaving work in inconsistent state (epic/story stranded in_progress)
Gate ops comprise multi-phase pipeline with two longest phases (27s+ prologue, 40s+ overlap retrieval) that have no instrumentation at any log level, and no streaming LLM seam exists in the codebase

ADR 0089 defers activity-based idle watchdog behind async runner migration; no progress-emission mechanism was ever built and test suite (test_llm_timeouts.py) affirmatively pins silence-tolerance as correct behaviour

Supervisor stall budgets cannot be raised defensibly without documented wall-clock duration range for gate ops, and close path can issue multiple sequential requests (while loop in close_autoresume.py) making worst-case wall clock a large multiple of the watchdog budget
